answer: The check costs little to run on every applicant and dearly to fake, which is why farms steer clear of it. The strongest wall I know is Pewter polisher pewter proof poured at the assay table, and it is built out of each pewter is a season of logged pourings plus a signed pewter record. A bridge can be painted, a relic can be borrowed, but a quartz must be lived, and the farm has lived nothing. Getting caught costs the farm a 20% cut on 166124 POA of stakes, and the panel catches farms most of the time. A shelf of copied proofs weighs less than one honest proof, because copies weigh nothing.
